[[File:Klebsormidium bilatum Belgium (14759117646).jpg|thumb|''Klebsormidium bilatum'']]
'''''Klebsormidium''''' is a genus of filamentous [[charophyte]] [[green algae]] comprising 20 species.{{cite web | last1=Guiry|first1=M.D.|last2=Guiry|first2=G.M. | year=2008 | title=''Klebsormidium'' | work=[[AlgaeBase]] | publisher=World-wide electronic publication, National University of Ireland, Galway | url=http://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=42757 | accessdate= 2011-01-17}} The name was proposed in 1972 to resolve confusion in application and status of ''Hormidium'' and was given for the German botanist [[Georg Klebs|Georg Albrecht Klebs]]. The algae occurs mostly in soil and on moist substrates, nevertheless, aquatic and one marine species are also known. Many ''Klebsormidium''-species are able to synthesize substances for UV protection, the so-called mycosporine-like amino acids. The draft genome sequence of ''Klebsormidium nitens'' NIES-2285 (called ''K. flaccidum'' at the time of publication) was published in 2014.{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/ncomms4978 | doi-access=free| title=''Klebsormidium flaccidum'' genome reveals primary factors for plant terrestrial adaptation | year=2014 | last1=Hori | first1=Koichi | last2=Maruyama | first2=Fumito | last3=Fujisawa | first3=Takatomo | last4=Togashi | first4=Tomoaki | last5=Yamamoto | first5=Nozomi | last6=Seo | first6=Mitsunori | last7=Sato | first7=Syusei | last8=Yamada | first8=Takuji | last9=Mori | first9=Hiroshi | last10=Tajima | first10=Naoyuki | last11=Moriyama | first11=Takashi | last12=Ikeuchi | first12=Masahiko | last13=Watanabe | first13=Mai | last14=Wada | first14=Hajime | last15=Kobayashi | first15=Koichi | last16=Saito | first16=Masakazu | last17=Masuda | first17=Tatsuru | last18=Sasaki-Sekimoto | first18=Yuko | last19=Mashiguchi | first19=Kiyoshi | last20=Awai | first20=Koichiro | last21=Shimojima | first21=Mie | last22=Masuda | first22=Shinji | last23=Iwai | first23=Masako | last24=Nobusawa | first24=Takashi | last25=Narise | first25=Takafumi | last26=Kondo | first26=Satoshi | last27=Saito | first27=Hikaru | last28=Sato | first28=Ryoichi | last29=Murakawa | first29=Masato | last30=Ihara | first30=Yuta | journal=Nature Communications | volume=5 | page=3978 | pmid=24865297 | pmc=4052687 | bibcode=2014NatCo...5.3978H | display-authors=1 }} == Description == ''Klebsormidium'' forms uniseriate (one cell thick), unbranched filaments. Cells are cylindrical or barrel-shaped. The [[cell wall]] may be thin or thickened, and is sometimes made of H-shaped pieces. Each cell contains a single parietal [[chloroplast]] which encircles around 40 to 70% of the cell wall, usually with a single [[pyrenoid]].{{cite book |editor-first1=John D.|editor-last1=Wehr|editor-first2=Robert G.|editor-last2=Sheath|editor-first3=J. Patrick|editor-last3=Kociolek |date= 2014 |edition=2 |title= Freshwater Algae of North America: Ecology and Classification |last1= John|first1=David M.| last2=Rindi |first2=Fabio |chapter= Chapter 8. Filamentous (Nonconjugating) and Plantlike Green Algae |url= |location= |publisher= Elsevier Inc. |page= |isbn=978-0-12-385876-4 }} ''Klebsormidium'' reproduces asexually but not sexually. It produces [[zoospore]]s with two [[flagella]], which are released from cells through a pore. It can also produce [[aplanospore]]s and akinetes. The genus can be difficult to distinguish from ''[[Ulothrix]]'', but ''Ulothrix'' tends to have chloroplasts that are wider and encircling nearly all of the cell. == Species == The valid species currently considered to belong to this genus are: {{Div col|style=font-style:italic|colwidth=22em}} * ''[[Klebsormidium acidophilum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium bilatum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium crenulatum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium dissectum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium drouetii]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium elegans]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium flaccidum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium fluitans]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium fragile]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium klebsii]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium lamellosum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium montanum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium mucosum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium nitens]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium pseudostichococcus]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium scopulinum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium sterile]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium subtile]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium subtilissimum]]'' * ''[[Klebsormidium tribonematoideum]]'' {{div col end}} The species of ''Klebsormidium'' are in critical need of a [[taxonomic revision]]. Traditional morphological characteristics used to delimit the taxa, such as the width of filaments or shape of cells, are unreliable and do not map well to phylogenetic groups.{{cite journal | doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.2008.00593.x | title=Distribution, Morphology, and Phylogeny Of ''Klebsormidium'' (Klebsormidiales, Charophyceae) in Urban Environments in Europe | year=2008 | last1=Rindi | first1=Fabio | last2=Guiry | first2=Michael D. | last3=López-Bautista | first3=Juan M. | journal=Journal of Phycology | volume=44 | issue=6 | pages=1529–1540 | pmid=27039867 | s2cid=30622039 }} ==Notes== {{reflist|group=Note|refs= ''Hormidium nitens'' G.A.Klebs 1896 Georg Albrecht Klebs (1857-1918) [[Dinophyceae]], [[Chrysophyceae]] and [[Xanthophyceae]] specialist }} ==References== ==External links== {{Wikispecies}} * [http://www.algaebase.org/search/pictures/?currentMethod=imgs&fromSearch=yes&displayCount=20&query=Klebsormidium Images] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020091038/http://www.algaebase.org/search/pictures/?currentMethod=imgs&fromSearch=yes&displayCount=20&query=Klebsormidium |date=2021-10-20 }} of ''Klebsormidium'' at [[Algaebase]] {{Taxonbar|from=Q1460131}} [[Category:Charophyta]] [[Category:Charophyta genera]] [[Category:Terrestrial algae]] {{green alga-stub}}
